keyVerseText: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun נַעֲרָה (naʻărâh) is the feminine form of נַעַר (naʻar), which primarily denotes a young person or servant. While נַעַר often refers to a boy or youth, נַעֲרָה specifically identifies a girl or young woman, encompassing a range from infancy through adolescence and into marriageable age. This root connection highlights a focus on youthfulness and service, suggesting not only physical age but also a social role within the community.
usageInScripture: The term נַעֲרָה appears 63 times in Scripture, predominantly translated as 'damsel,' 'the damsel,' or 'young woman.' Its usage consistently emphasizes the youth and often the unmarried or marriageable status of a female individual, as seen in various narrative contexts. The frequent occurrence of the word in the Pentateuch and historical books underscores its importance in describing young women in familial, social, and sometimes servile roles, reflecting both innocence and responsibility.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding נַעֲרָה enriches our grasp of biblical personhood, especially the dignity and role of young women in God’s covenant community. The word’s range from infancy to marriageable age reminds us of God’s care for individuals at every stage of life and the significance of purity and readiness in His redemptive plan. In a Christ-centered perspective, the concept of a 'damsel' who serves or is entrusted with tasks can be seen as a foreshadowing of the Church’s purity and service, called to be a bride prepared for the Bridegroom, Jesus Christ. This word invites believers to honor God’s design for youthfulness, service, and covenant relationship.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 24:14 uses נַעֲרָה to describe the young woman chosen by divine providence to be Isaac’s wife. The verse emphasizes the damsel’s willingness to serve, as she offers water to both the servant and his camels, symbolizing kindness and suitability for God’s plan. Here, נַעֲרָה conveys not just youth but also the character and readiness of the woman God appoints, illustrating how God works through faithful individuals to fulfill His promises.
